Chapter 01 — Kazharitrarivar Nayanar

Tiruchitrambalam. Periyapuranam, Part 937, composed by the divine Sekkizhar Peruman. Varkonda Vanamulaiyal Sarukkam. Kazharitrarivar Nayanar Puranam. In the Tiruttondar Puranam, which is the Periyapuranam composed by the divine Sekkizhar Peruman, the Puranam of Kazharitrarivar Nayanar is the 37th Puranam, following the Puranam of Siruttonda Nayanar. The Peruman who is praised by all as Cheraman Peruman Nayanar is Kazharitrarivar Nayanar. This section speaks about his sacred Puranam. This Sarukkam, named Varkonda Vanamulaiyal Sarukkam, is not the Sarukkam corresponding to the sixth verse in the Tiruttondattogai composed by our Lord Sundaramurthy Swamigal. Sundaramurthy Swamigal has praised Cheraman Peruman Nayanar. He praises him saying, "I am a servant to Kazharitrarivar, whose generosity is like the rain-bearing clouds." The sixth sacred verse of Tiruttondattogai, "Varkonda Vanamulaiyal Umaipangan Kazhale Maravadu Kallerinda Sakkiyarkkum Adiyen Sirkonda Pugazh Vallal Sirappulikkum Adiyen Sengattangudi Meya Siruttondarkku Adiyen," continues with Sundaramurthy Swamigal singing, "Karkonda Kodai Kazharitrarivarkkum Adiyen." Therefore, in this Sarukkam, the Puranam of Sakkiya Nayanar, the Puranam of Sirappuli Nayanar, and then the Puranam of Siruttonda Nayanar are followed by the fourth Puranam, which is the Puranam of Kazharitrarivar Nayanar. In the compendium Tiruttondattogai, Sundaramurthy Swamigal praises him thus. The meaning of "Karkonda Kodai Kazharitrarivarkkum Adiyen" is that "I am a servant to Kazharitrarivar Nayanar, whose generosity surpasses that of the rain-bearing clouds." "Kar" means cloud. "Kolluthal" means to conquer or surpass. To surpass the nature of the cloud. The nature of the cloud is to give without expecting anything in return. The Tirukkural states, "Kaimaru Venda Kadappadu Marimattu En Attungollo Ulaku," meaning, "What return can the world make to the rain, which gives without expecting anything?" Similarly, the cloud helps all living beings in this world by showering rain. What return can these living beings make to such a cloud? Likewise, those who are like these clouds, their generosity and charity, they do not expect any return. What return can the living beings who benefited from their generosity make to those who gave that charity? This is what the Tirukkural states. Our Cheraman Peruman Nayanar, Kazharitrarivar Nayanar, surpassed even the generosity of such clouds. Surpassing the generosity of the clouds is due to his special quality of aligning with the nature of Shiva. Moreover, there is a hint here that all clouds obey his command. Accordingly, even today, in the mountainous country of Cheraman Peruman Nayanar, rain falls without fail according to the season, and with the help of that rain, we see rice and other crops growing even on elevated lands. In our plains like Tamil Nadu, we store river water in dams and reservoirs, and then channel it through canals to cultivate rice and other crops. However, in the mountainous country of Cheraman Peruman Nayanar, due to the abundant rain that falls without fail, we see rice and other crops growing even on elevated lands without the need for dams or reservoirs to store water. Therefore, it also means that the clouds obey our Lord's command. The Tirumugappasuram also praises this, saying, "Paruvappon Muppadi ena." The Nayanar's sacred name is Kazharitrarivar. The divine Sekkizhar Peruman himself will explain the meaning of this name in the 3761st sacred verse of the Puranam. Thus, the meaning of the phrase "Karkonda Kodai Kazharitrarivarkkum Adiyen," sung by Sundaramurthy Swamigal in the compendium Tiruttondattogai, is established. Now, in the detailed work Tiruttondar Tiruvandadi, Nambiyandar Nambi praises the Nayanar in two sacred verses, numbers 44 and 45. The 44th sacred verse is: "Mannar Piran Edir Vannaan Udal Uvar Ooriya Neettra En Piran Tamar Pola Varudhalum Tazh Vananga Enna Piran Adiyanna En Adiccheran Ennum Thennar Piran Kalaritrarivon Ennum Cheralane." Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, having been crowned, is riding on an elephant, making a procession through the city. At that time, he sees a washerman coming towards him, carrying a bundle of alkaline earth on his back. Due to the rain, the alkaline earth in the bundle carried by the washerman, who was coming on the elephant, dissolved and seeped, making his entire body white. Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, recognizing this form as the sacred attire of a devotee, quickly dismounted from the elephant and bowed to the washerman. The washerman, his mind disturbed, bowed and said, "O King, I am Adi Vannaan." Cheraman Perumal Nayanar heard this and bowed, saying, "I am Adi Cheran. You have done me the favor of reminding me of the sacred attire, which is like the sacred ash, by your form." Cheraman Perumal Nayanar had great devotion to the sacred ash. This is what Nambiyandar Nambi explains in this first sacred verse, the first verse praising Cheraman Perumal Nayanar in the Tiruttondar Tiruvandadi. Seeing the washerman, whose body was soaked with alkaline earth and appeared as if smeared with sacred ash, coming like a devotee of Shiva before the crowned king, Cheraman Perumal Nayanar bowed at the washerman's feet. The washerman said, "My Lord, I am Adi Vannaan." To this, Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, who had the power to say, "I am Adi Cheran," is the Chera king known as Kalaritrarivon. In the 45th sacred verse, Nambiyandar Nambi praises Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, saying that his heart did a good deed by serving that king, Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, who was a warrior who had conquered Kama, and who drove his horse to go before the big, mad white elephant given by Lord Shiva to Nambigal, the Lord of Thennavalur, who was a Chera king. We will see this sacred history at the end of the Periyapuranam. When Sundaramurthy Swamigal ascended to the mountainous country and made a request for liberation from the sacred place of Tiruvanchaikkalam, Lord Shiva sent a white elephant from Tirukkailayam. Sundaramurthy Swamigal ascended to Tirukkailayam on that white elephant, and before him, our Cheraman Perumal Nayanar also reached Tirukkailayam by driving his horse. We will see that history in the Vellana Sarukkam, the concluding Sarukkam. Nambiyandar Nambigal Swamigal praises this in this sacred verse. Thus, the detailed work Tiruttondar Tiruvandadi praises Cheraman Perumal Nayanar. Now, in the extensive work Tiruttondar Puranam, also known as Periyapuranam, the divine Sekkizhar Peruman describes this Puranam of Kalaritrarivar Nayanar in 175 sacred verses. We reflected on the Puranam of Eyarkon Kalikkama Nayanar, and we saw that it mostly contained the sacred history of Sundaramurthy Swamigal. In this Puranam of Kalaritrarivar Nayanar also, we see the next part of the sacred history of Sundaramurthy Swamigal. Cheraman Perumal Nayanar became friends with Sundaramurthy Swamigal due to divine grace. Later, we will see in this Puranam that both of them together visited many sacred places. In the extensive work Periyapuranam, the Puranam of Kalaritrarivar Nayanar is the 37th Puranam. It is the fourth Puranam in the seventh Sarukkam, Varkonda Vanamulaiyal Sarukkam. This section describes the history and character of Kazharitrarivar Nayanar. The first sacred verse is: "Maveetrirunda Perunchirappin Mannum Tonmai Malainattu Paveetrirunda Palpugazhar Payilum Iyalbil Pazhampatithan Seveetrirundar Tiruvanchaikkalamum Nilavi Cherarkula Koveetrirundu Murai Puriyum Kulakkomathur Kodungolur Enbadu Tiruppadal." The mountainous country, which is ancient and established with great glory where the goddess of wealth resides, is a region ruled by the Chera kings, one of the three ancient Tamil kings. Kodungolur is the great capital city where the Chera kings have ruled for generations. Near it is the sacred place called Tiruvanchaikkalam, where Lord Shiva resides and bestows grace. We see that this mountainous country, the Chera royal lineage, and this ancient city of Kodungolur were highly praised in ancient Tamil poems. The mountainous country is a land where Mahalakshmi, the goddess of wealth, always resides with brilliance. We extensively reflected on it as Parasuraman Perunadu in the Puranam of Viranminda Nayanar. Similarly, it is an ancient city with many glories, praised in ancient Tamil poems, where the Chera royal family and its people have been practicing their traditions for generations. Ancient Tamil poems like Patittruppattu, Silappathikaram, Purananuru, and other Sangam literature extensively speak about the generosity of the Chera kings. Patittruppattu specifically praises the Chera kings. Silappathikaram was sung by Ilango, a prince of the Chera lineage. It specifically speaks about the greatness of Cheran Senguttuvan. In Purananuru, there are many Chera kings praised, starting from Perunsorru Udiyan Cheralathan and Mandaran Cheral Irumborai. In all these poems, the glory of the Chera kings is extensively spoken about. Most of these praise poems are about the generosity of the Chera kings. Such a mountainous country is the land known as Kerala today. The ancient city there, where our Lord Shiva resides with brilliance and bestows grace, is the sacred place called Tiruvanchaikkalam. Kodungolur and Tiruvanchaikkalam are honorably referred to as a single city. We see that Tiruvanchaikkalam and Kodungolur are praised together in the Tevarams. It is praised as Anjaikkalam Kodungolur in the Tevaram. Kodungolur was the capital of the Chera kings. Tiruvanchaikkalam was the temple they worshipped. Therefore, in this first sacred verse, we see the greatness of the mountainous country, the greatness of the city of Kodungolur, the greatness of the city of Tiruvanchaikkalam, their ancient history, the richness of their flags, and many other things being praised. We extensively reflected on the richness of this country, the mountainous country, in the Puranam of Viranminda Nayanar. Since the divine Sekkizhar Peruman sang about it very extensively there, he briefly mentions it here. The city of Kodungolur is located near Tiruchur, which is called Tiruchippeyur. Currently, the Kodungallur Bhagavathi Amman temple is very famous. Near it is Tiruvanchaikkalam, which is now called Vanchikkalam. Tiruvanchaikkalam is a unique sacred place in the mountainous country. Kodungolur also has the name Mahodai. It served as the capital of the Chera kings for a long time. Their palace is also there. There is also a Shiva temple, which is a Tevaram Vaipputhalam. In that Shiva temple, to the southeast of Lord Shiva's sanctum, there is a temple built by Cheran Senguttuvan for Kannagi. It is widely known as Kodungallur Bhagavathi. When Cheraman Perumal Nayanar was a prince, he did not stay in the palace but stayed in Tiruvanchaikkalam and performed sacred service to Lord Shiva. That place is known as Cheraman Purambu. The government has erected a memorial pillar there and marked its boundaries to protect it. This place called Cheraman Purambu is on the Kulasekaram road, which leads to the southern sea port of the temple. Tiruvanchaikkalam is the place where Parasurama worshipped Lord Shiva to cleanse himself of the sin of killing his mother and siblings. This is the place where Sundaramurthy Swamigal made a request for liberation, and Lord Shiva sent a white elephant from Kailash with Indra, Vishnu, Brahma, and sages. Sundaramurthy Swamigal ascended to Kailash on that white elephant, and on the way, he sang the Tevaram Tiruppathikam called Tirunodithanmalai. This is the place where Varuna announced it to Anjaiyar Appar, as per Sundaramurthy Swamigal's command. Tiruvanchaikkalam is famous for the fact that when Cheraman Perumal Nayanar saw Sundaramurthy Swamigal going to Kailash on an elephant, he chanted Shiva's mantra into his horse's ear, mounted it, and went to Kailash with Sundaramurthy Swamigal through the sky. Here, Nambigal and Cheraman Perumal Nayanar are worshipped together, seated on the same pedestal. The images of the elephant and horses on which they went to Kailash are painted on the gopuram entrance. The Lord of Dance, Nataraja Peruman, who made the sound of anklets audible to Cheraman Perumal Nayanar at the end of his daily puja, is enshrined in the Tiruvanchaikkalam Mahadevar temple. Thus, these are the glories of Kodungallur, the capital of our Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, and the sacred place of Tiruvanchaikkalam near it. Let us continue to reflect. Tiruchitrambalam.

Chapter 02 — Kazharitrarivar Nayanar

Tiruchitrambalam. Periyapuranam, Part 938, composed by the divine Sekkizhar Peruman. Varkonda Vanamulaiyal Sarukkam. Kazharitrarivar Nayanar Puranam. The second sacred verse. The sounds of various arts rising in the morning, the trumpeting of elephant calves, the gentle humming of bees rising from the groves, the sounds of horses swirling with pride, the sounds of the palai vipanchi (a type of lute), and the sounds of drums accompanying songs and dances, all rising to drown the sound of the sea, thus shining with wonder. The divine Sekkizhar Peruman sings about the greatness of the city of Vanchi, known as Kodungolur. In the morning, the sounds of the Vedas and other arts being practiced are heard there. Early morning is the time for practicing arts, so the sounds of the Vedas and artistic knowledge being practiced are heard in the morning. The trumpeting of elephant calves is heard. Elephants are in the outskirts, but their calves are in the city. They are trained. The trumpeting of such elephant calves is heard. The gentle humming of bees rising from the groves is heard. The sounds of horses neighing and swirling with pride are heard. Here, the historical note that the Nayanar will later reach Tirukkailayam on one of these horses comes to our mind. The sounds of drums accompanying songs and dances are heard there. Palai Vipanchi is a type of lute. Palai has seven types and 103 variations. The details of these can be found in music treatises. Palai refers to the lute. Vipanchi also means a type of Kurinji lute. The western sea surrounds this city. The sound of the sea waves is also heard. The third sacred verse. In every house, abundant wealth and blossoming joy shine. In every street, crowded with people, many places of charity abound. In every mansion adorned with suitable ornaments, the glory of Saivism is proclaimed. In every place filled with abundant resources, countless treasures are accumulated. In this sacred verse, the divine Sekkizhar Peruman explains the state of the four ultimate goals of life – dharma, artha, kama, and moksha – in this country. He has prioritized joy first, then dharma, then the Saiva truth that grants liberation, and finally wealth. So, he arranges them in the order of joy, dharma, liberation, and wealth. All living beings generally desire and find joy desirable. Therefore, he places joy first, and that joy should come through dharma. It should be enjoyed. So, he places dharma next to it, in accordance with the saying that joy comes from dharma. Then, he places the imperishable joy of ultimate liberation third, following the order of its attainment. In accordance with the saying that "what sages and kings desire is achieved through gold," and since wealth is a means for dharma, joy, and the monasteries that show the path to liberation, the divine Sekkizhar Peruman places wealth last, following the order of cause and effect. The houses in this country are filled with wealth. That wealth was earned through dharma. Wealth can also be interpreted as offspring, meaning a country with good children and good people. Because there is this wealth in every house, joy blossoms and shines. In every street crowded with houses, acts of charity are performed. In every monastery where worthy devotees reside, the true principles of Saivism are expounded. Proclaiming the truth of Saivism means teaching according to the rules and making it known through conduct. Here, it is concluded that the Saiva path alone can show the path to liberation. Now, in the places where abundant resources are accumulated, there are many places where valuable goods, wealth, jewels, gold, silver, and other such things are stored. The fourth sacred verse.

The four castes, which do not deviate from the path prescribed by the Vedas and uphold excellent conduct, are established in their respective dharmas in this mountainous country, surrounded by a large moat and groves of mango, bakula, and sarala trees. This prosperous city is also known in the world by the name Mahodai, the city of the garlanded kings. The four excellent castes, who do not deviate from the methods of the path prescribed in the Vedas and who uphold excellent conduct, are established in their respective dharmas in this mountainous country. These four varnas, namely Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Sudra, and their conduct, are prescribed in the Vedas. These are essential for the good state of a city. In these days, conflicting views about these have spread and caused confusion among the people. The true meaning of these has been obscured, and false propaganda about their nature is currently being carried out. The belief that castes and their adherence to good conduct are essential for the well-being of society is a traditional view held by our ancestors. For those who observe closely, it will become clear that the deviation from these distinctions is the cause of the troubles we see today. Thus, there are varna distinctions, but there are no quarrels or conflicts among them. Therefore, we see that dharma flourished, and wealth flourished. Now, that city, Kodungolur, is also known by the name Mahodai. It has the glory of being the capital of the Chera kings. That city is a prosperous city surrounded by groves. The city of Mahodai is a prosperous city surrounded by groves dense with rows of mango trees, bakula trees, and sarala trees. We can still see this sight today. The fifth sacred verse. In that ancient city, with groves of fragrant flowers, Perumakothaiyar was born by the great penance performed by the Chera lineage, who had mighty elephants, and the world, by the grace of Lord Shiva, so that the power of Saivism, which establishes dharma by removing the destructive Kali according to the traditional rules, may flourish. In this sacred verse, the divine Sekkizhar Peruman blesses us with the news of the sacred birth of Cheraman Perumal Nayanar. In that ancient city, surrounded by groves of fragrant flowers, Perumakothaiyar was born by the grace of Lord Shiva, by the great penance performed by the Chera lineage, who had mighty elephants, and the world, so that the power of Saivism, which establishes dharma by removing the destructive Kali according to the traditional rules, may flourish. Perumakothaiyar. Kothaiyar is the traditional name of the Chera kings. Thus, our Nayanar takes birth. Let us continue to reflect. Tiruchitrambalam.

Chapter 03 — Kazharitrarivar Nayanar

Tiruchitrambalam. Periyapuranam, Part 939, composed by the divine Sekkizhar Peruman. Varkonda Vanamulaiyal Sarukkam. Kazharitrarivar Nayanar Puranam. Our Nayanar, Perumakothaiyar, was born. The sixth and seventh sacred verses. The great city, due to the special festival of the sacred birth, was filled with overflowing joy, and as the anointing with ghee was performed, a shower of celestial flowers rained down from the sky, filling it with auspicious sounds, and all living beings on this great earth were filled with increasing joy. Our Nayanar, born to uphold the Saiva path on earth, grew up with the love that came from his previous good deeds, devoted to the feet of the Lord with the shining third eye on his forehead. With inner love, he did not engage in royal duties but performed sacred service at Tiruvanchaikkalam, the sacred place of the Lord with clear water in his matted locks. The people of the wealthy city of Kodungolur, filled with great joy due to the special festival of the sacred birth of our Nayanar, Perumakothaiyar, celebrated with an anointing ceremony using ghee. A shower of celestial flowers rained down from the sky. All living beings on this great earth were filled with increasing joy due to the sacred birth of our Nayanar. Our Nayanar, as the Chera king, not only alleviated the sufferings of humans but also those of non-human beings, and he is going to rule. He wished to understand the language and meaning of non-human beings. Through this, he wanted to ensure that their sufferings were also alleviated under his rule, and that non-human beings also lived happily. For this, our Nayanar prayed to the Lord and received the boon to understand the thoughts of non-human beings, and then he ruled. Therefore, all living beings in this world rejoiced due to the sacred birth of our Nayanar. Due to the sacred birth of our Nayanar, all these beings are going to live and attain salvation by following the Saiva path. Our Nayanar, who took birth for the salvation of beings, was devoted to the feet of Lord Shiva with the love that came from his previous good deeds. His heart was completely filled with love for the Lord. This inherent love is the love that came with him from his previous good deeds. We saw in the Puranam of Tirukkannappadeva Nayanar that the accumulation of past good deeds leads to endless joyful love. Sivagnanabodham states that it is realized through penance. Now, the adhikarana states that knowledge arises in these souls through past good deeds. Although he was born into a royal lineage, our Nayanar did not engage in royal duties but performed sacred service at Tiruvanchaikkalam, where Lord Shiva resides with brilliance. It is very rare to have love for Lord Shiva from a young age. It is even rarer for those born into a royal lineage to perform service to Lord Shiva instead of royal duties. All these things do not come without previous penance. Now, the divine Sekkizhar Peruman sings about the sacred services performed by our Nayanar in the next two sacred verses. The eighth and ninth sacred verses. Knowing that the nature of the world and the nature of kingship are not permanent, he would rise early, bathe in water, and also bathe in the sacred white ash. He would perform many duties in the sacred Nandavanam, bring flowers and buds, arrange them with joy to adorn the Lord, bring sacred water for ablution, apply sacred unguents, and joyfully perform sacred sweeping with love. He would also perform other sacred services with great devotion, reciting sacred hymns with a unified mind and devotion, and thus he spent his days.

These two sacred verses, composed by the divine Sekkizhar Peruman, describe the sacred service performed by our Nayanar. Our Nayanar realized that this worldly life and royal life are impermanent. He understood that worldly life and royal life are perishable and not permanent, and therefore he performed the permanent sacred service to God. He rises early in the morning, bathes in water, and then bathes in the purifying sacred white ash. Bathing in vibhuti or sacred white ash is called Basma Snanam. Applying sacred ash all over the body is considered bathing in sacred ash. There are eight types of bathing. They are Varunam, which is bathing in water. The second is Agneyam, which is applying sacred ash related to fire, called Basma Snanam. We also see that Basma Snanam is a part of Sandhyavandanam. Now, the third type of bathing is Mantram, which is chanting mantras. The fourth is Manasam, which is Pranava Dhyanam. The fifth type of bathing is called Divya Mahendram. It is walking seven steps eastward in the rain that appears with the sun's rays. That is Divya Mahendram Snanam. The sixth type of bathing is called Marutam or Vayavyam. This is walking against the wind, allowing the dust from the hooves of a cow to fall on one's body. That Snanam is called Maruta Snanam or Vayavya Snanam. The sixth type of bathing is Parthiba Snanam. This is applying mud from a Shiva temple or a river, mixed with water, or sprinkling that mixed water. This is called Parthiba Snanam, the seventh type of bathing. Now, the eighth type of bathing is called Gauravam. Bathing in the sacred water from the feet of the Acharya is called Gaurava Snanam. Bathing in the sacred water from the feet of the Acharya, sprinkling it on oneself, and consuming it are all part of this eighth type of Gaurava Snanam. Thus, there are eight types of Snanam. The first four types of Snanam are considered Nitya (daily), and the next four types are considered Naimittika (occasional). The details of these are clearly explained in the book Saiva Bhushanam. Here, our Nayanar is said to have bathed in the sacred white ash, which refers to Agneya Snanam. Therefore, it is sacred white ash, purifying vibhuti. We have seen the Tiruneetru Tiruppathikam, which states that "cleanliness is ash." Therefore, the message here is that only white ash is to be worn. Thus, after bathing in water in the early morning and then performing Agneya Snanam by bathing in sacred white ash, he performs duties in the sacred Nandavanam. The Nayanar performs gardening duties such as watering trees and plants and weeding. Then, he brings flowers and buds and joyfully arranges them to adorn the Lord with garlands. The flowers should be freshly bloomed. The buds should be picked at the appropriate time for blooming, according to the time they are to be offered to the Lord. As we have seen, "Kamizh Mugai Alarum Velai Deiva Nayakarkku Saathum Tiruppallithamam," he brings flowers and buds and arranges garlands in various forms such as Tamam, Pinaiyal, and Kanni. Having arranged them, he goes to the Tiruvanchaikkalam temple, where Lord Shiva resides, and performs all the sacred temple services such as Tirumanjanam (sacred ablution), Tirualagu (sacred cleaning), and Tirumezhukku (sacred sweeping) for Anjaikkalathu Appar Mahadevar. He also performs Tiruppattu Tiruppani (reciting sacred hymns). All these are the sacred services performed by our Nayanar, Perumakothaiyar, when he was a prince, residing in Tiruvanchaikkalam. "Tirumanjanamum Konarndu" means bringing and adding water for the Lord's sacred ablution. "Tirumezhukku Saathi" means lovingly and joyfully sweeping and cleaning the temple courtyard. It also means cleaning the inside and outside of the temple, including the sacred walls and mandapams. Other services include lighting sacred lamps. He performs these with great desire and love. He performs them with a unified mind. In addition, he recites sacred hymns. Our Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, Kazharitrarivar Nayanar, was skilled in composing hymns in praise of the Lord. His compositions, sacred texts, and hymns are compiled in the Tirumurais. Therefore, he recites the sacred hymns he composed in praise of the Lord. He also recites the Tirumurai hymns, such as Ammaiyar Tiruppathikams, Tirumantiram, Aludaiya Pillaiyar Tevaram, and Tirunavukkarasu Peruman Tevarams. The sacred services mentioned earlier are to be performed with the body. Reciting sacred hymns is done with the voice. It is said that he performs all these with a unified path and a unified mind. This refers to the service performed with the mind. Thus, the Nayanar performs sacred service with the three instruments of mind, speech, and body. The Tevaram composed by Tirunavukkarasu Peruman states, "Nilaiperumara Ennudhiye Nenje Nee Vaa Nithalum Emperan Udaya Koyil Pukku Pularvathan Mun Alagittu Mezhukkum Ittu Poomalai Punainthethi Pugazhndu Padi Talaiyara Kumpittu Koothum Adi Sankara Saya Potri Potri Enrum Alai Punal Ser Senjadaiyam Aathi Enrum Arurara Enrenre Alara Nille." The Tiruvachakam Tiruchathakam states, "Amaru Un Tiruvadikke Agankuzhaiyen Anburuken Poomalai Punainthethen Pugazhnduraiyen Putthezhir Koman En Tirukkoyil Thooken Mezhuken Koothaden Samarare Viraikindren Sathurale Sarvane." The sacred words of Tayumanava Swamigal state, "Aduthuvathum Paaduvathum Anandamaga Ninnai Theduvathum Nin Adiyar Seigai Paraparame." When we read about all the sacred services undertaken by our Nayanar, all these sacred words come to our mind. Now, the tenth sacred verse. The king named Sengolporaiyan, whose generosity was like the clouds, ruled the city, which was surrounded by a moat filled with water and a long mountain range, under the shade of his white umbrella, and then he renounced the world and embraced penance. At that time, in the city of Kodungolur, a Chera king named Sengolporaiyan was ruling. It was during the same period that our Nayanar was born and was performing sacred service to the Lord at Tiruvanchaikkalam, not staying in the palace of Kodungolur, the capital. The city of Kodungolur is a city surrounded by the sea on one side, filled with water. On the other side, it is a city with high, large mountains. Therefore, the sea serves as a moat, and the mountains surround it like a fortress. Thus, this country is a land surrounded by the sea and filled with mountains. Therefore, the sea itself is a natural moat, and the mountains are natural fortresses surrounding that mountainous country. The king who ruled that sacred city was named Sengolporaiyan. He ruled under the shade of his white umbrella. Above that white umbrella was the abundant shade of the clouds, symbolizing his great generosity. Under that, the white umbrella, and under that, this king ruled. His reign was so excellent that Sekkizhar Peruman describes it by saying that this king ruled under two shades. One is the shade of generosity, and the other is the shade of the umbrella. Among them, the shade of generosity is above, and the shade of the white umbrella is below it. What does it signify that the king ruled under the white umbrella, which is a special emblem for crowned kings? Just as an umbrella protects the person under it from the troubles of sun, rain, and cold, so too it is the king's duty to protect his country from suffering, increase its joy, and rule it appropriately. This is one of the special emblems for crowned kings. The white umbrella is a symbol that the king alone is entirely responsible for the welfare of the country. We see that Srimat Madhava Sivagnana Munivar, in his commentary on the eighth sutra of Sivagnanabodham, states that the king is like the first cause, the great white umbrella, which is the root cause of all creation and is uniquely his, not belonging to anyone else. This is how this king ruled well under that white umbrella. Now, the shade of generosity. This is the benefit of dharma that comes from generosity. The cloud benefits this world by showering rain without expecting anything in return. This king benefits even more than the cloud. Therefore, the special boon for this country is the cloud that rains abundantly and regularly, and the other is the king's generosity. As we have already seen, ancient Tamil texts like Patittruppattu and Purananuru extensively praise the generosity of the Chera kings. We note here that the names of Chera kings such as Peruncheral Irumborai and Ilancheral Irumborai come from such a glorious king named Sengolporaiyan. The meaning of this name is one who rules with a just scepter. Such a king renounces this worldly rule and embraces the discipline of penance. He goes to Tapovanam. It is a very special and excellent tradition of the Chera kings, which we can still see today, for kings to voluntarily renounce their rule and embrace asceticism. We see the traditions of the Kochi kings. We will also see it in the Puranam of Aiyadigal Kadavarkon Nayanar. It is a very special glory of the kings of our Bharatavarsha to renounce the highest authority while still being crowned kings and embrace the great state of penance. However, if we look at the meanness of contemporary people, who, even in their very old age, desperately cling to positions with very little authority for a few days, the greatness of our ancestors becomes very clear. After that king renounced his rule and went to perform penance, the right to rule now belongs to our Cheraman Perumal Nayanar. Therefore, all the ministers go to our Kazharitrarivar Nayanar, Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, and request him to accept the rule. Let us continue to reflect. Tiruchitrambalam.

Chapter 04 — Kazharitrarivar Nayanar

Tiruchitrambalam. Periyapuranam, Part 940, composed by the divine Sekkizhar Peruman. Varkonda Vanamulaiyal Sarukkam. Kazharitrarivar Nayanar Puranam. The Chera king renounces his royal duties and goes to Tapovanam to perform penance. All the ministers request our Cheraman Perumal Nayanar to accept the kingship. The 11th sacred verse. After the king, who was to rule according to the established tradition, went to the forest to perform penance, the ministers, who were wise and learned in statecraft, deliberated for some days and then, following the ancient tradition, went to our Nayanar, who was engaged in sacred service at Tiruvanchaikkalam, the sacred place of the moon-crowned Lord. The ministers, who were sharp-witted, deliberated for some days after the king, who was to rule according to the established royal lineage, went to the forest to perform penance as mentioned before. They studied all the texts pertaining to the succession of kingship according to the royal tradition and understood the matter clearly. Having deliberated and understood, they went to Tiruvanchaikkalam and approached our Nayanar, who was performing sacred service there. The 12th sacred verse. Having approached him, they bowed before him and said, "The right to rule this mountainous country, which is filled with waterfalls, has come to you by the traditional law of succession, so please accept the crown without blemish." Thus spoke the truthful ministers, praising him. The ministers went before our Nayanar, bowed, and submitted their request. They said, "The right to rule this mountainous country, which is filled with waterfalls, has come to you by the traditional law of succession, so please accept the crown without blemish." They stood praising him. The custom of the mountainous country, the law of the mountainous country, is the traditional way of succession, where the right to inherit comes through the maternal line. This is also known as Marumakkathayam. In Tamil Nadu, in other kingdoms like those of the Cholas and Pandyas, the male line of succession, where the son inherits from the father, is followed. But in the mountainous country of the Cheras, the tradition is that the succession comes through the female line, through the sister. We can still see this in the state of Kerala today. We learn about this in their laws. It is because of this system of Marumakkathayam that we see women having more rights and privileges in this mountainous country of Kerala. We also see the name Pen Malayala (Female Kerala) being used. Thus, the ministers stood submitting their request. It is customary to praise the king or anyone to whom a request is being made before making the request. Here, the Nayanar is not only a king but also a great person who is deeply devoted to Lord Shiva. Therefore, it was necessary to praise him. Accordingly, they made their request, praising him. The 13th sacred verse. "If there is grace to rule without deviation from the state of love, even though this is an impediment to the sacred service that brings increasing joy, I will take leave from the Lord who wears bones and snakes, and I will know His will," said the Nayanar, bowing before the Lord and submitting his request with the grace of the Lord. Our Nayanar, Kazharitrarivar Nayanar, felt in his heart that these ministers were making such a request, which was an impediment to his sacred service that brought ever-increasing joy. He thought, "If there is grace from the Lord to rule without deviating from the state of love for Shiva, I will take leave from the Lord and know His will." He entered the temple, bowed before the Lord, and submitted his request. The intention of Cheraman Perumal Nayanar was that the ministers were requesting him to accept the kingship, which was an impediment to his sacred service to Lord Shiva. This was the Nayanar's inner feeling. Although he was born with the right to rule, our Nayanar did not desire those rights and worldly pleasures. From a young age, he did not stay in the palace in Kodungolur but stayed in Tiruvanchaikkalam and performed sacred services to Lord Shiva, as we have seen. Now, even though he was offered the kingship, the Nayanar's heart remained in its previous state. It is the nature of Shiva's devotees to despise worldly pleasures such as kingship and to dedicate themselves to praising the Lord's feet and serving His devotees. The Tiruvachakam states, "Bhogam Vendi Vendilen Purandara Inbamum," meaning, "I do not desire pleasures, nor do I desire worldly happiness." The 11th Tirumurai Tiruvidaimarudur Mummanikkovai states, "Indirac Chelvamum Ettu Siththiyum Vanthuli Vanthuli Marutthanan Odungi," meaning, "When the wealth of Indra and the eight siddhis came, I rejected them and moved away." The Periyapuranam states, "Koodum Anbinil Kumbidalai Anri Veendum Venda Viralil Vilanginar," meaning, "They shone in their desire not for liberation, but for bowing with increasing love." We see countless such sacred sayings. We see the nature of Shiva's devotees in this way. Therefore, he thought, "If there is grace from the Lord to rule without deviating from the state of love for Shiva, I will take leave from the Lord and know His will." He decided to submit his request to the Lord and know His will. There are specific times and places for submitting requests to the Lord, according to the rules of Shiva worship. The rules of Shiva worship and temple visitation also state this. The Nayanar's inner desire was that service to the Lord is the sacred service that brings increasing joy. Therefore, it is understood that the nature of kingship is not of that kind. Joy comes from being immersed in the grace of Shiva. That joy is born of love. We have seen that the Lord Himself declared the nature of devotees as those who find joy in love. We have seen that the Mother requested "iravatha inba anbu" (undying joyful love). The Tiruvachakam states, "Inbame Ennudaiya Anbe," meaning, "Joy is my love." We will see that Aiyadigal Kadavarkon Nayanar, despising kingship as a source of trouble, entrusted it to his beautiful son and became one who delighted in performing sacred service. Therefore, the Nayanar requested that if he were to rule, it should be with the grace that would allow him to do so without deviating from the state of love for Shiva. Indeed, the Nayanar's heart believed that royal pleasures and worldly pleasures are not permanent. If so, why did he not immediately refuse the ministers' request? Why did he not refuse immediately, but instead went to the Lord and submitted his request to know His will? This is because the Nayanar realized that it was the Lord's grace that had guided him to Shiva's service and would continue to do so without fail. However, the Nayanar also realized that it was the Lord's grace that had placed him in the royal lineage, brought the kingship to him through tradition, and thereby placed these worldly duties upon him. Therefore, he also thought that he should not refuse these duties. In the Kambar Ramayanam, we see Kambar stating that Sri Rama understood that the responsibility of kingship was a duty. Therefore, he wondered whether to continue with "En Kadan Pani Seithu Kidappathe" (My duty is to serve and remain) or to accept the kingship that had come by grace without opposing it and perform worldly duties according to the Lord's grace. He was in doubt as to what was to be done. He feared accepting the kingship because it would be an impediment to his sacred service. At the same time, caste, lifespan, and pleasures are the results of past karma. Therefore, refusing those duties would be acting against divine grace. Therefore, he also feared refusing the kingship that had come by grace. He also feared accepting it. The Nayanar arose, saying, "If divine grace commands me to rule without deviating from the state of love, I will submit my request to the Lord and know His will." Here, we should reflect on the Tiruvachakam, "Vendathakkathu Arivoy Nee Venda Muzhuvathum Thruvoy Nee Vendi Niyatha Arul Seithai Yanum Athuve Vendinallal Vendum Parisu Onru Undu Ennil Athuvum Ninthan Viruppanre," meaning, "You know what is to be desired, you give everything that is desired, you have bestowed grace without my asking, I too desire only that, if there is anything else to be desired, that too is your will." We have read about the history of Tirugnanasambandar Peruman submitting his request to know the Lord's will before going to debate with the Jains at Madurai Tirualavayil. We see Tirunavukkarasu Peruman submitting his request, "Ponnar Tiruvadikku Onru Undu Vinnappam Potri Seyyum En Avi Kappatharku Ichai Undel," meaning, "I have a request for your golden feet, if you wish to protect my soul." Therefore, even if divine grace led him to accept the duty of kingship, the Nayanar's intention was that it should be without deviating from his love for the Lord. Therefore, he submits his request to the Lord in this manner. Our Nayanar submits his request, asking what the message of divine grace is, what the command of divine grace is. Let us continue to reflect. Tiruchitrambalam.

Chapter 05 — Kazharitrarivar Nayanar

Tiruchitrambalam. Periyapuranam, Part 941, composed by the divine Sekkizhar Peruman. Varkonda Vanamulaiyal Sarukkam. Kazharitrarivar Nayanar Puranam. The Nayanar submits his request to the Lord, asking for the command of divine grace. The 14th sacred verse. "Having received the right to rule, and with boundless love and devotion, he received the understanding to know all that everyone speaks, and also received endless courage, unfailing generosity, and all the qualities proper to a king, such as an army and vehicles." By the grace of the Lord, Cheraman Perumal Nayanar received the Lord's command. Our Nayanar understood that accepting the right to rule and remaining in the path of love was the Lord's grace. He had requested to rule without deviating from his love for the Lord. The Lord granted him exactly what he desired. In addition, the Lord Himself bestowed upon the Nayanar the necessary components for such a rule. Kings are not just rulers for the people under them. They have the responsibility to protect all other living beings. Therefore, kings have the responsibility to protect non-human beings as well as humans. Only if they have the understanding to know the languages spoken by all those beings can they protect non-human beings. Therefore, the Lord bestowed upon our Nayanar the understanding to know the languages and feelings of all people and all beings. In addition, this Nayanar was in a state of Sivayoga. For those who have attained Sivayoga, the sounds of all beings are contained within the Nada sound that is perceived. We have already seen the responsibility of kings to protect all living beings, including people, in the section on the greatness of the city. Therefore, our Nayanar was in such a state. That is why our Cheraman Perumal Nayanar chanted the Shiva mantra into his horse's ear, mounted it, and reached Tirukkailayam, as we will see in that history. Therefore, it was because he had the understanding to know the languages and feelings of all humans and all living beings that this Nayanar, Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, was given the sacred name Kazharitrarivar. The 15th sacred verse. "Having received that grace, he bowed and came out, and though ruling would be a blemish to his sacred service, by the grace of the Lord, he agreed to the ministers who had requested him to wear the glorious crown, and the worthy ministers bowed and joyfully undertook that task." As mentioned before, Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, having received the divine grace, bowed and came out of the temple. It is his duty to follow the path shown by grace. Therefore, even though ruling would be an impediment to his sacred service, having received the Lord's grace, he gave his consent to the ministers who had requested him to wear the glorious crown. Those ministers bowed at the Nayanar's feet and joyfully undertook the desired tasks. The 16th sacred verse. "On the auspicious day and hour of his coronation, with all the necessary and glorious auspicious items arranged, and all the auspicious rituals performed, Kazharitrarivar, who understood the nature of righteous justice that brings joy to all living beings, crowned himself with a single crown that was suitable for both worlds." This is the sacred verse. On that auspicious day, at that auspicious hour destined for coronation, with all the special auspicious items arranged and all the auspicious rituals performed, the Nayanar crowned himself. He is Kazharitrarivar, who protects this world by understanding the nature of righteous justice that brings joy to all living beings, classified as high-caste and low-caste. He crowned himself with a single crown that was suitable for both this world and the next. The 17th sacred verse. "Having circumambulated the Lord's temple and bowed before Him, he mounted the mighty elephant, and with the white umbrella and fly-whisk held by his loyal attendants, he circumambulated the beautiful city, and then he saw a washerman in front of him, carrying a bundle of alkaline earth on his shoulder." Having circumambulated the Lord's temple and bowed before Him, touching the ground, he mounted the mighty elephant. With the white umbrella and fly-whisk held by his attendants, he circumambulated the city. Therefore, we see that the coronation took place in the palace where the Nayanar resided in Tiruvanchaikkalam. Because the divine Sekkizhar Peruman sings that immediately after the coronation, he circumambulated the Lord's temple and bowed before Him, we can understand that the coronation ceremony took place in the palace where the Nayanar resided in Tiruvanchaikkalam. Immediately after the coronation, he went to the temple, worshipped the Lord, and then set out. This period, that is, before he accepted the kingship, the Nayanar had established a separate monastery in Tiruvanchaikkalam and resided there, performing all the temple services. That place is still there today, a short distance south of the temple (which people now call Tiruvanchikulam). The researcher of the Kochi government discovered it and erected a memorial pillar there, inscribing it as the place where Cheraman Perumal Nayanar's palace was located. They have written it as "The site of the palace of Sri Saint Cheraman." Four Shiva lingams are also embedded there. Even today, the Kochi kings, after their coronation, first worship at Tiruvanchaikkalam and then present an elephant as a special custom, as written by Sivakavimani Aiya. We see that the custom of the king riding an elephant and circumambulating the city is still prevalent in the mountainous country of Kochi and Travancore. We also see the tradition of holding umbrellas and fly-whisks over the elephant. It is customary for the crowned king to circumambulate the city in the same attire. Now, our Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, after his coronation, worshipped at the Tiruvanchaikkalam Appar temple and then set out from there on an elephant in the same attire to Kodungolur, the capital. This is the city procession. As he was proceeding, he saw a washerman carrying a bundle of alkaline earth on his shoulder. The 18th sacred verse. "Seeing the washerman, whose body was whitened by the alkaline earth that had dissolved in the rain, as a devotee of the Lord with the sacred hand, he dismounted from the elephant with the excellent forehead ornament and quickly went and bowed to him with overflowing love." We saw that the washerman was carrying a bundle of alkaline earth. Due to the rain, the alkaline earth dissolved and seeped, making the washerman's body appear white. Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, realizing that this was the sacred attire of a devotee of the Lord, dismounted from the elephant he was riding. He dismounted from the elephant's neck and quickly went forward with great love and bowed to the washerman with folded hands. The alkaline earth carried by the washerman had dissolved in the rain and seeped, making his body appear white. Even today, we see that it rains many times in a single day during the rainy season in that country. The appearance of whiteness on the body reminded Cheraman Perumal Nayanar of the sacred attire of a devotee of Shiva. That was the Nayanar's state of maturity. The sacred attire of a devotee is determined by the brilliance of the sacred ash. We saw this in the history of Enathinatha Nayanar. We also saw the Puranam of Meypporul Nayanar, who considered even cunning people who smeared sacred ash all over their bodies as his own. We also saw in the Puranam of Siruttonda Nayanar that when no devotee was found to feed the Bhairava devotee, he requested to be accepted as a devotee of Shiva solely for having applied sacred ash. Therefore, the whiteness on the washerman's body was not due to sacred ash. Nevertheless, it reminded the Nayanar of sacred ash and showed him the sacred attire of a devotee. Even today, there are people who, upon seeing the whiteness of sacred ash, are reminded of the whiteness of lime. Therefore, immediately upon seeing the sacred attire of the devotee, bowing with love is a sign of true devotion, as stated in Sivagnanabodham, "Vedamum Aran ena Thozhume," meaning, "Even the Vedas worship it as Shiva." Immediately upon seeing the sacred attire of the devotee, he quickly dismounted from the elephant's neck with love and bowed to him. It is forbidden to bow while seated on a vehicle. Therefore, he quickly dismounted and went quickly to the washerman and bowed to him with folded hands. This shows that the Nayanar was always devoted to Shiva worship, without giving any thought to his worldly status as a king, or that he was crowned, or that he was making a city procession, or that he was riding on an elephant. Thus, the Nayanar bowed to the washerman. The 19th sacred verse. "Seeing the Chera king bowing to him, the washerman's mind was disturbed, and he bowed before him and said, 'Who do you take me to be? I am Adi Vannaan.' The Chera king replied, 'I am Adi Cheran. You have reminded me of the sacred attire of sacred ash. Go without worry.'" Seeing the Chera king bowing to him, the washerman's mind was disturbed, and he bowed before him and said, "O King, who do you take me to be, that you do this? I am Adi Vannaan, your servant, the washerman." He thought that the king had mistakenly taken him for someone else and bowed, and so he revealed the truth. Therefore, the washerman's tact in pointing out the king's mistake, his humility in stating his true status, and his noble mindset and culture are indicated. This indicates the high worldly civilization of the Tamils in those days. To that washerman who spoke thus, our Nayanar, Cheraman Peruman, said, "I am Adi Cheran." This place fills us with wonder at the Nayanar's exalted love, his high worldly civilization, and his timely and sweet words. To his statement, "I am Adi Vannaan," the king replied, "I am Adi Cheran." Cheraman Perumal Nayanar continued to say to the washerman, "You have reminded me of the sacred attire, which is the brilliance of sacred ash. Therefore, you may go without worry." Therefore, he means, "Do not think in any way that you have caused an interruption in the king's city procession or that you have become the cause of any untoward incident. Continue on your way." Thus, Cheraman Perumal Nayanar replied. Seeing the king's sacred service, all the ministers folded their hands above their heads and praised him. Let us continue to reflect. Tiruchitrambalam.

Chapter 06 — Kazharitrarivar Nayanar

Tiruchitrambalam. Periyapuranam, Part 942, composed by the divine Sekkizhar Peruman. Varkonda Vanamulaiyal Sarukkam. Kazharitrarivar Nayanar Puranam. The 20th sacred verse. Seeing the king's sacred service, all the wise ministers bowed with folded hands above their heads and praised him. The king mounted the mighty elephant and entered the gate of the palace, adorned with golden jewels, after circumambulating the ancient city with its streets filled with mansions adorned with flags, so that the auspicious decorations might shine. Seeing the king's sacred service, all the wise ministers bowed with folded hands above their heads and praised him. The king mounted the mighty elephant and entered the gate of the palace, adorned with golden jewels, after circumambulating the ancient city with its streets filled with mansions adorned with flags. Flags are essential features of all great cities. Kodungolur is such a city, filled with mansions. The king, after circumambulating that city, arrives at the gate of his palace, which is located in Kodungolur. Since the crowned king is arriving, the people welcome him grandly with decorations and auspicious items such as full pots, incense, and lamps. The 21st sacred verse. "Having dismounted from the elephant, he ascended the exalted throne in the jeweled hall, and as the white umbrella cast its shade above him, and the beautiful-eyed women waved white fly-whisks before him, and many flowers were scattered, the great king, the Nayanar, sat enthroned, praised by the mighty kings." Having dismounted from the elephant, he ascended the exalted throne in the jeweled hall. As the white umbrella cast its shade above him, and the women waved white fly-whisks before him, and many flowers were scattered, the great king, the Nayanar, sat enthroned, praised by the mighty kings. All the tributary kings bowed, scattering flowers and praising him. Thus, the great king sat enthroned, praised by the tributary kings. The 22nd sacred verse. "He ruled the earth, protecting the world, with the generous Cholas and the rightful Pandyas, as great three kings, upholding justice according to the Manusmriti, bringing tribute from countless kings, eradicating internal and external enemies, and fostering the radiant light of sacred ash and the growth of the Vedas." This sacred verse describes how our Cheraman Perumal Nayanar ruled the earth, protecting the world. He ruled alongside the generous Cholas, who protected the world, and the rightful Pandyas, as great three kings. He upheld justice according to the Manusmriti, received tribute from countless kings, eradicated internal and external enemies, and fostered the radiant light of sacred ash and the growth of the Vedas. The crowned kings, the three Tamil kings, are the Cheras, Cholas, and Pandyas. These royal lineages have existed since the time of creation, according to tradition. These rulers ruled over the entire Tamil Nadu. At times, their rule extended up to the Himalayas and even across the seas. Therefore, the divine Sekkizhar Peruman praises them as rulers who protected the world and whose rule was eternal, stating that these three lineages ruled the world as crowned kings. "Valavar" refers to the Cholas. "Chezhiyar" refers to the Pandyas. The divine Sekkizhar Peruman refers to the Chola kings as "Ulaku Purakkum Kodai Valavar" (generous Cholas who protect the world). The Chola lineage was a dynasty that followed the Saiva path without deviation. The Chola lineage was also characterized by its ability to establish this world without deviation from that path. Generosity is that which brings both spiritual and physical well-being to life. Such generous people are the "Valavars," the wealthy ones. They are the Chola kings. Now, when referring to the Pandyas, the divine Sekkizhar Peruman refers to them as "Urimai Chezhiyar" (rightful Pandyas). This indicates that they were the rightful ones, the lineage that intermarried with the Cholas. We will see in this history that during the time of Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, when the Chola king, who had married the daughter of the Pandya king, was staying in Madurai, the Chola and Pandya kings met and rejoiced with our Cheraman Perumal Nayanar and Sundaramurthy Swamigal when they came to Madurai. In addition, we will see the history of these three kings coming together and worshipping at many sacred places. Therefore, we see that during this period, these three kings were in friendship, without internal conflicts or other differences. We also see that the tributary kings and petty chieftains under our Cheraman Perumal Nayanar, who was a great emperor, paid their respective tributes. Cheraman Perumal Nayanar ruled by eradicating internal and external enemies. External enemies are those who are hostile and unfriendly kings. Internal enemies are those who come from within oneself, from one's own people, from thieves, from living beings, and from oneself. Our Nayanar ruled by establishing the submissive kings who paid tribute on the right path and by punishing and removing the disobedient ones. We see that in those days, there were no governmental enmities such as anarchy, treason, various parties, or factions among the people of Tamil Nadu, which we see today. This is one meaning of internal and external enemies. Now, the inner meaning is that internal enemies are those that arise from ignorance, lust, and other evils, and external enemies are those that arise from the five senses. He ruled by establishing the people on the right path through good conduct, good teachings, and other means, so that they would not suffer from internal enemies such as ignorance and lust, and by removing the evils that come from the five senses, which are external enemies, and by making the people free from ego and attachment, he ruled. Therefore, the divine Sekkizhar Peruman sings that he ruled this world, eradicating these internal and external enemies, fostering the radiant light of sacred ash, and the growth of the Vedas. As per "Veda Neri Thazhaithonga Migu Saivathurai Vilanga" (May the Vedic path flourish and the great Saiva path shine), our king ruled so that Vedic disciplines and Saiva Agamic disciplines would prevail well. Let us continue to reflect. Tiruchitrambalam.
